newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan expels Indian embassy official.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan expels Indian embassy official.

text.p: Pakistan expelled an Indian High Commission (embassy) official on Tuesday accusing him of spying in an apparent tit-for-tat move between the two arch rivals, a mission spokesman said.

He said a Pakistani order accused the Indian staff member A.C. Sinha of involvement in "activities incompatible with his status", a diplomatic euphemism for spying, and ordered him to leave the country by October 4.
No Pakistani comment was immediately available.
On Monday, India said it had expelled a Pakistani diplomat, Nur Mohammad Mattoo, on a similar charge as the two sides also traded charges of kidnapping one another's diplomats.
The Indian mission official said Sinha was kidnapped outside his home in Islamabad by 15 Pakistani intelligence agents on Monday morning and was released about 15 hours later.

The Pakistani High Commission in New Delhi said in a statement on Monday that it had protested to the Indian foreign ministry after Indian intelligence agents abducted the Pakistani diplomat in Delhi on Saturday and kept him in illegal detention for 16 hours.
Both sides have rejected the spying charges.
India and Pakistan have fought three wars since their independence from British rule in 1947, two of them over the disputed Himalayan region of Kashmir.
